title: One Man Flees Putin’s Draft: An Update

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做 DJ 时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的藏品去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: This week, The Daily is revisiting some of our favorite episodes of the year and hearing what's happened in the time since they first ran.
sentences.zh: 本周，《每日新闻》将重温我们今年最喜欢的一些剧集，并了解它们首次播出后发生的事情。

sentences.en: Today, we return to one man's choice to flee Russia rather than being part of Vladimir Putin's draft and find out what's happened since he left the country.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们回顾一位男士选择逃离俄罗斯而非参与弗拉基米尔·普京征兵的决定，并了解他离开该国后发生了什么。

sentences.en: It's Friday, December 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 12 月 30 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Tell me your name, your, just your first name, because I know the sensitivities, your age, and where you live.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你的名字，只说名字就行，因为我知道这很敏感，还有你的年龄以及你住在哪里。

sentences.en: My name is Kirill.
sentences.zh: 我叫基里尔。

sentences.en: I'm 24, and I live in Moscow, OblaSt.
sentences.zh: 我 24 岁，住在莫斯科州。

sentences.en: So, Kirill, going back to the beginning of the war, when Putin first ordered the invasion of Ukraine on February 24th, take me back to that moment in your life.
sentences.zh: 那么，基里尔，回到战争刚开始的时候，当普京在 2 月 24 日下令入侵乌克兰时，带我回到你生命中的那一刻。

sentences.en: What did you think when you saw that?
sentences.zh: 你看到那个消息时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: On the 24th, I woke up not very early, kind of like usual, around 11 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 24 号那天，我醒得不算太早，和平常差不多，大概是上午 11 点左右。

sentences.en: My friend in the morning said that war had begun.
sentences.zh: 我朋友早上告诉我战争开始了。

sentences.en: If I'm being honest with you, I don't actually remember that day very much,
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不记得那天太多的细节了，

sentences.en: because I didn't fully understand and comprehend the magnitude of what had happened and how horrible it would all be.
sentences.zh: 因为我当时并没有完全理解和领会所发生之事的严重性，以及这一切会有多可怕。

sentences.en: I remember that I went home that day and began talking to my parents.
sentences.zh: 我记得那天我回家后开始和父母谈话。

sentences.en: I didn't really want to talk about it with my parents, because I don't talk about political topics with them.
sentences.zh: 我其实不想和父母谈论这件事，因为我不和他们聊政治话题。

sentences.en: We have very different points of view, and I like to avoid those things with them.
sentences.zh: 我们的观点差异很大，我喜欢避开这些话题。

sentences.en: My parents aren't exactly part of that really toxic part of the public that's really, really for this war, that, you know, puts Z-stickers on the back of their car.
sentences.zh: 我的父母并不属于那种极度支持这场战争、在车后贴上“Z”字贴纸的极端公众群体。

sentences.en: They're not those people.
sentences.zh: 他们不是那样的人。

sentences.en: It's hard for me to quite describe to you, but I will say that they are people who try very hard not to notice the lawlessness that is going on around them.
sentences.zh: 我很难向你准确描述，但我会说他们是那种极力试图忽视周围无法无天现象的人。

sentences.en: And I came to them and said, the war is a catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 我走到他们面前说，这场战争是一场灾难。

sentences.en: There's no reason in the world that one country should attack another country.
sentences.zh: 世界上没有任何理由让一个国家去攻击另一个国家。

sentences.en: It just seemed so clear to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说太显而易见了。

sentences.en: And they said, what do you mean by war?
sentences.zh: 他们却说，你说的战争是什么意思？

sentences.en: Are you saying that they're lying to us and you're the one who knows the truth?
sentences.zh: 你是说他们在对我们撒谎，而你是那个知道真相的人吗？

sentences.en: Did you argue?
sentences.zh: 你们吵架了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we argued very badly.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们吵得很凶。

sentences.en: I love my parents.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的父母。

sentences.en: That's clear.
sentences.zh: 这一点很明确。

sentences.en: We each set our position and never returned to the topic, because we understood we just had different points of view.
sentences.zh: 我们各自表明了立场，之后再也没有回到这个话题，因为我们明白彼此的观点就是不同。

sentences.en: So, the time started going by, yes, and I basically turned into a person that was just constantly updating the news on my phone.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，是的，我基本上变成了一个不断在手机上刷新闻的人。

sentences.en: The strange thing was, there was a war.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，战争确实发生了。

sentences.en: I could see it happening.
sentences.zh: 我能看到它正在发生。

sentences.en: But in the first three months, I didn't really feel it at all.
sentences.zh: 但在最初的三个月里，我一点也没感觉到。

sentences.en: Nothing around me changed.
sentences.zh: 我周围的一切都没有改变。

sentences.en: And that is what was most disturbing for me, the contraSt.
sentences.zh: 而这正是让我感到最不安的地方，这种反差。

sentences.en: A number of years ago, a very famous rock musician said this about the Chechen War.
sentences.zh: 多年前，一位非常著名的摇滚音乐人曾这样评价车臣战争。

sentences.en: He said the most disturbing thing was being at the war and seeing the mud and the death and getting on an airplane and flying back and landing in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他说最令人不安的是，身处战场看到泥泞和死亡，然后坐上飞机飞回莫斯科着陆。

sentences.en: And seeing people walking around on the streets and children playing on jungle gyms and people shopping.
sentences.zh: 看到街上人们走来走去，孩子们在攀爬架上玩耍，人们在购物。

sentences.en: The most frightening thing is for people to have their lives keep going on and not feel the pain that is being caused in this other place.
sentences.zh: 最可怕的事情是，人们的生活照常继续，却感受不到在另一个地方所造成的痛苦。

sentences.en: It really just didn't concern our lives.
sentences.zh: 它真的与我们的生活无关。

sentences.en: It really didn't concern our lives.
sentences.zh: 它真的与我们的生活无关。

sentences.en: Where were you the moment that you heard about this so-called partial mobilization?
sentences.zh: 当你听到所谓的“部分动员”消息时，你在哪里？

sentences.en: It was two days ago.
sentences.zh: 那是两天前的事了。

sentences.en: I woke up 15 minutes before my alarm clock and I saw the news.
sentences.zh: 我在闹钟响前 15 分钟醒来，看到了新闻。

sentences.en: I saw the news in the face of the president.
sentences.zh: 我看到了总统发表讲话的新闻。

sentences.en: I saw the banner headline with little lightning bolts next to it that was telling me this was important, that he was announcing a partial mobilization.
sentences.zh: 我看到了带有闪电标志的头条新闻，告诉我这很重要，他正在宣布进行部分动员。

sentences.en: And I understood that given my health, my age and my former military service, that I fit the criteria 100%.
sentences.zh: 我明白，考虑到我的健康状况、年龄和曾经的兵役经历，我完全符合征召标准。

sentences.en: How did you feel in that moment?
sentences.zh: 那一刻你感觉如何？

sentences.en: I guess I just felt this sense of resignation, kind of futility.
sentences.zh: 我想我只感到一种宿命感，一种徒劳感。

sentences.en: Like, I was just going to go to work, but I was going to be called up in this draft and go to war.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我本来要去上班，但却要被征召入伍去打仗。

sentences.en: What was the feeling in your heart?
sentences.zh: 你心里是什么感觉？

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: I felt this emptiness.
sentences.zh: 我感到一种空虚。

sentences.en: Not anger.
sentences.zh: 不是愤怒。

sentences.en: Kind of almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 几乎什么感觉都没有。

sentences.en: I just thought, what do I do next?
sentences.zh: 我只是想，接下来我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Because I realized at that moment that the war had finally come to me.
sentences.zh: 因为那一刻我意识到，战争终于降临到我头上了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 探索太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60 款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝 175 年来帮助你了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Kirill, you talked about your military service.
sentences.zh: 基里尔，你谈到了你的兵役经历。

sentences.en: How long did you serve in the military?
sentences.zh: 你在军队服役了多久？

sentences.en: I was there for a year.
sentences.zh: 我在那里待了一年。

sentences.en: When I graduated from my technical school, I was drafted and I didn't have money to buy my way out of it.
sentences.zh: 从技术学校毕业时，我被征召入伍，但我没钱买通关系逃避兵役。

sentences.en: The only people who really go to the army are the ones that can't buy their way out of it.
sentences.zh: 真正去参军的人，都是那些没钱逃避的人。

sentences.en: It's not a choice to go off to defend the fatherland.
sentences.zh: 去保卫祖国并不是一种选择。

sentences.en: It's about poverty.
sentences.zh: 这是关于贫困。

sentences.en: And the desire to feed their families.
sentences.zh: 以及养家糊口的渴望。

sentences.en: So going back to when Putin first announced the mobilization, what did you start to do?
sentences.zh: 那么回到普京首次宣布动员的时候，你开始做什么了？

sentences.en: What was the first thing?
sentences.zh: 第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: First, I started researching where I could go to get out.
sentences.zh: 首先，我开始研究我能去哪里逃离。

sentences.en: Where I could go to get out that wouldn't require a visa and wouldn't require a lot of money because I don't have a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 去哪里可以不用签证，也不需要很多钱，因为我没多少钱。

sentences.en: Physically, I started to feel bad.
sentences.zh: 身体上，我开始感到不适。

sentences.en: I had a really bad headache.
sentences.zh: 我头痛得厉害。

sentences.en: I was very afraid.
sentences.zh: 我非常害怕。

sentences.en: I'm not going to hide it from you.
sentences.zh: 我不打算对你隐瞒。

sentences.en: I was terrified.
sentences.zh: 我吓坏了。

sentences.en: Then I just sat down,
sentences.zh: 然后我坐下来，

sentences.en: breathed in, caught my breath, and I went to work.
sentences.zh: 深呼吸，平复了一下，然后去上班了。

sentences.en: I got there, and there were several other young men who were in the same category as me.
sentences.zh: 我到了那里，还有其他几个和我情况一样的年轻人。

sentences.en: We sat there, and we were drinking coffee together and kind of laughing and just talking about it, and it felt better.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在一起喝咖啡，开着玩笑聊着这件事，感觉好了一些。

sentences.en: We were talking about what was the information out there, who was going to try to leave, what we were going to try to do.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了现有的信息，谁打算尝试离开，我们打算尝试做什么。

sentences.en: As the hours went by and I was texting with my friends and watching the news, it became very clear how many lies had been told.
sentences.zh: 随着时间流逝，我一边和朋友发短信一边看新闻，很明显他们撒了多少谎。

sentences.en: They said they wouldn't draft students, and we saw many students being called up.
sentences.zh: 他们说不会征召学生，但我们看到许多学生被征召了。

sentences.en: They said they wouldn't draft people who were in their 50s and 60s, and we saw many people in their 50s and 60s being called up.
sentences.zh: 他们说不会征召 50 多岁和 60 多岁的人，但我们看到许多 50 多岁和 60 多岁的人被征召了。

sentences.en: So it became clear that this was something that was really going to affect everybody.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这件事真的会影响到每一个人。

sentences.en: Then I began to feel really in danger that they're going to come for me right now.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始感到真正的危险，觉得他们随时会来找我。

sentences.en: And I saw when the news had been announced about a partial mobilization, all of these people going out to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 我看到部分动员的消息宣布时，所有这些人都走上街头抗议。

sentences.en: I wanted to go out to the protest, but I stayed home because I was very afraid that if they got me, if the police got me, that would lead to my drafting.
sentences.zh: 我想去参加抗议，但我待在家里，因为我非常害怕如果我被抓了，如果警察抓到我，那就会导致我被征召。

sentences.en: How do you feel about that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I feel regret that I didn't go.
sentences.zh: 我感到后悔，后悔没去。

sentences.en: It was as if I had just kind of abandoned the mission, as if I was saying,
sentences.zh: 就好像我放弃了任务，就好像我在说，

sentences.en: OK, young women, young men, you people not of drafting age, you go out and say your piece and say it on my behalf.
sentences.zh: 好吧，年轻的女性、年轻的男性，你们这些还没到征召年龄的人，你们去表达你们的观点，替我发声吧。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm dramatizing this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我有点戏剧化了。

sentences.en: I don't want to be dramatizing this.
sentences.zh: 我不想把这件事戏剧化。

sentences.en: I don't want you to be thinking that I'm in some sort of terrible situation.
sentences.zh: 我不想让你觉得我处于某种可怕的境地。

sentences.en: It's just a lot of people are in this situation now.
sentences.zh: 只是现在很多人都处于这种境地。

sentences.en: I'm warm.
sentences.zh: 我很温暖。

sentences.en: I feel good.
sentences.zh: 我感觉还好。

sentences.en: I'm under a roof.
sentences.zh: 我有遮风挡雨的地方。

sentences.en: The thing that I'm feeling right now has nothing, nothing in comparison to the thing that people are feeling who are in the war.
sentences.zh: 我现在感受到的东西，与那些身处战争中的人所感受到的相比，根本不算什么。

sentences.en: I don't want to have any comparison drawn there.
sentences.zh: 我不想做任何比较。

sentences.en: So two days after Putin's announcement, my father got a call.
sentences.zh: 普京宣布消息两天后，我父亲接到了一个电话。

sentences.en: A friend of his in the police station gave him a call.
sentences.zh: 他在警察局的一个朋友打来的。

sentences.en: And he said, there's a draft notice for your son tomorrow for the next day.
sentences.zh: 他说，明天或后天会有一张给你的儿子的征兵通知单。

sentences.en: And that he was going to bring it over.
sentences.zh: 而且他打算把它送过来。

sentences.en: I had this feeling of helplessness.
sentences.zh: 我有一种无助感。

sentences.en: I didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: And I've been at work for the past couple of days.
sentences.zh: 过去几天我一直待在工作的地方。

sentences.en: You live at work now?
sentences.zh: 你现在住在工作的地方？

sentences.en: Yes, I'm living at work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我住在工作的地方。

sentences.en: You're sleeping there?
sentences.zh: 你在那里睡觉？

sentences.en: You're brushing your teeth there?
sentences.zh: 你在那里刷牙？

sentences.en: You're taking a shower there?
sentences.zh: 你在那里洗澡？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: There's everything for this.
sentences.zh: 这里什么都有。

sentences.en: Because I'm working with a professional organization.
sentences.zh: 因为我是在一家专业机构工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, all of the above.
sentences.zh: 是的，实际上，以上这些都有。

sentences.en: And it's actually not that hard because I'm working in an organization that is for homeless people.
sentences.zh: 而且其实并不难，因为我工作的机构是为无家可归者服务的。

sentences.en: So there's lots of creature comforts and things that we have for people around.
sentences.zh: 所以我们周围有很多为人们提供的生活便利设施。

sentences.en: In particular, yeah.
sentences.zh: 特别是这样，是的。

sentences.en: That's the only thing I can get this information.
sentences.zh: 这是我获取信息的唯一途径。

sentences.en: I'm hiding here because I don't want to be in a place where people recognize me and people could come and give me this draft notice.
sentences.zh: 我躲在这里，因为我不想待在人们能认出我、能来给我送征兵通知单的地方。

sentences.en: The way that it has been working is that people are being given these things on the streets, at protests, when they come out of the metro.
sentences.zh: 现在的运作方式是，人们在街上、抗议活动中、或者从地铁出来时被发放这些东西。

sentences.en: And this is something that I'm trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 这是我试图避免的事情。

sentences.en: So I've been here at work and I don't think they will find me or get me if I don't go out.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直待在工作的地方，如果我不出去，我想他们找不到我也抓不到我。

sentences.en: There were a few people in my company that met the criteria for the draft.
sentences.zh: 我公司里有几个人符合征召标准。

sentences.en: We put a few plans together, which we're now trying to carry out.
sentences.zh: 我们制定了一些计划，现在正试图实施。

sentences.en: Our co-workers are trying to gather all of our documents and figure out from embassies and from different places where potentially we could go and get a visa to get out.
sentences.zh: 我们的同事正在努力收集我们所有的文件，并从大使馆和不同地方弄清楚我们可能去哪里申请签证离开。

sentences.en: I'm hugely grateful to them, but I understand that that variant is really unlikely, that it's basically not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激他们，但我明白那个方案真的不太可能，基本上是不可能实现的。

sentences.en: So if that doesn't happen and I don't think it will, then the second thing we're thinking of is to get to the border with Kazakhstan and we're hoping that the border doesn't close.
sentences.zh: 所以如果那行不通，而且我认为行不通，那么我们考虑的第二件事是前往哈萨克斯坦边境，我们希望边境不会关闭。

sentences.en: When would you go to Kazakhstan?
sentences.zh: 你打算什么时候去哈萨克斯坦？

sentences.en: So I'll probably be in this work space that I've been in for the past couple of days until the 28th of September.

sentences.en: It's from their support that I can feel completely comfortable and confident living my life in
sentences.zh: 正是因为他们的支持，我才能在

sentences.en: Tashkent.
sentences.zh: 塔什干的生活中感到完全舒适和自信。

sentences.en: They've helped me monetarily, financially.
sentences.zh: 他们在金钱和经济上帮助了我。

sentences.en: Oh, wow, Kiril.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，基里尔。

sentences.en: My father came to see me in
sentences.zh: 我父亲来看我了，在

sentences.en: Uzbekistan.
sentences.zh: 乌兹别克斯坦。

sentences.en: That was about three weeks after I left.
sentences.zh: 那是我离开后大约三周。

sentences.en: He just came and we walked around the city and just talked.
sentences.zh: 他来了，我们在城市里走走，只是聊了聊天。

sentences.en: I'm trying to think of just kind of how, how you're feeling right now, how you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我在想，你现在感觉如何，过得怎么样。

sentences.en: I mean, it was such a huge change to your life, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对你的生活来说是一个巨大的改变，对吧？

sentences.en: Leaving your country, at least for now, and starting to live this kind of strange new life in Uzbekistan.
sentences.zh: 至少目前为止，离开你的国家，开始在乌兹别克斯坦过这种奇怪的新生活。

sentences.en: Are you happy that you left?
sentences.zh: 你后悔离开吗？

sentences.en: I was very glad to, not to leave, but to be apart and away from all of that mobilization, from everything that was happening.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴，不是说离开，而是远离了所有的动员，远离了正在发生的一切。

sentences.en: But after I'd been gone for about two weeks, I started to feel like, okay, maybe, maybe I can go back.
sentences.zh: 但离开大约两周后，我开始觉得，好吧，也许，也许我可以回去。

sentences.en: Maybe I can go back.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以回去。

sentences.en: It just felt so sad to me that I was so far from my work, the people I love there, and from my parents.
sentences.zh: 离我的工作、我在那里爱的人以及我的父母那么远，让我感到非常难过。

sentences.en: But, you know, I've signed up for many channels and news sites, and I've been reading a lot, and now I'm coming to the realization that it was a little naive
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我订阅了许多频道和新闻网站，读了很多东西，现在我意识到，认为我一月份就能回去

sentences.en: thinking that I would be able to go back by January.
sentences.zh: 有点天真。

sentences.en: What do you mean, naive?
sentences.zh: 你说的天真是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because there's more and more news saying that either in December or in
sentences.zh: 因为有越来越多的新闻说，要么在十二月，要么在

sentences.en: January, there'll be yet another wave of mobilization.
sentences.zh: 一月，还会有另一波动员。

sentences.en: I'm thinking, you know, this is going to be for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我在想，你知道，这会持续很长时间。

sentences.en: It's not going to end in January, so that gives me a heavier heart.
sentences.zh: 它不会在一月份结束，所以这让我的心情更加沉重。

sentences.en: Are you sad?
sentences.zh: 你难过吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sad.
sentences.zh: 难过。

sentences.en: I really, really want to go back.
sentences.zh: 我真的、真的很想回去。

sentences.en: I just want to go back.
sentences.zh: 我只是想回去。

sentences.en: But I just want to say that, you know, I have a house.
sentences.zh: 但我只想说，你知道，我有一个家。

sentences.en: I have a place to live, unlike those
sentences.zh: 我有住的地方，不像那些

sentences.en: Ukrainians whose houses were destroyed.
sentences.zh: 房子被毁的乌克兰人。

sentences.en: I'm lucky.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运。

sentences.en: Пока, Kirill.
sentences.zh: 再见，基里尔。

sentences.en: Пока, пока.
sentences.zh: 再见，再见。

sentences.en: Пока.
sentences.zh: 再见。
